plot: Monday night in the pantry Lolly scrubs the sesame seeds off Bup and finds a round black burn mark on his back the size of Crispy, so everyone suspects Crispy burned him; Crispy threatens to leave for good and hides behind the flour bin, Bup's one try to drag him out ends with Pim falling into the flour and finding Walter's old tin, whose 1976 newspaper reveals the twist — Bup was the loaf who carried the little burnt roll Crispy out of the fire, the mark is from saving him; Crispy admits he hid out of guilt, Bup keeps his oldest friend, and the last line says the pot that started the fire had three dents like eyes.

script.title: Who Saved Bup From the Bakery Fire?

beats.say: Crispy, stop rolling away! What fire? Tell me what happened!
Not tonight, Bup. Some fires are better left cold.
New episode every day. Subscribe so you don't miss what happens next.
Monday night. The pantry. Bup still has sesame seeds stuck everywhere.
On the floor sits Mom's box from the old bakery.
Hold still, seed head. I'm scrubbing you clean for the window.
Ow! Gentle! My crust is fifty years old, apparently.
Lolly scrubs his back. Then she stops scrubbing.
Bup. There's a black mark on your back. A round one.
Fact. That mark is exactly the size of Crispy.
C-Crispy burned Bup? Our Crispy? The quiet one?
Crispy? He warms our toes every night. He'd never hurt anyone.
In the dark corner, two ember eyes look away.
Crispy, did you do this to me? Is that why you hide?
Ask me again, and I leave this house. For good.
Crispy rolls behind the big flour bin. Into the darkest corner.
Great. Now our grumpy rock is sulking behind the flour.
If he leaves, I'll never know what happened that night.
Then we need evidence. Mom's bakery box. Somebody climb in.
N-not me. Old boxes have spiders. And memories. Mostly spiders.
But Bup has one idea. He marches to the flour bin.
Crispy! Out! I'm the leader, and that's an order!
Crispy doesn't move. Bup pushes. Bup slips. Bup wobbles on the edge.
Pim jumps to catch him. And lands headfirst in the flour.
Pim comes up white. Totally white. A tiny bean ghost.
Pim! You look like a powdered donut with eyes!
D-don't laugh! There's something down here. An old tin!
Under the flour, a dented tin. Walter's name on the lid.
Inside: one newspaper page. Burnt at the corners. Nineteen seventy-six.
Fire at Walter's Bakery. A pot left on the stove all night.
The baker got out safe. And on the doorstep, he found…
Found what? Read it, Zeek! Every word!
His window loaf. Burnt on the back. Holding a tiny roll.
The tiny roll was black as coal. But it was alive.
A tiny black roll? Th-that sounds like somebody we know.
That mark isn't from Crispy hurting you, Bup.
It's from carrying him. Out of the fire.
B-but Crispy's at the back door! He's really leaving!
Bup runs. Seeds flying. All the way across the pantry floor.
Crispy, wait! I read it. I know what happened.
Then you know. You got burned because of me.
I was a new little roll. I rolled onto the hot tray.
You pulled me off. Your back took all the heat.
So you hid in the shadows all these years? For that?
You forgot. I never wanted you to feel you owed me.
Bup is quiet for a long time. Then he smiles.
I don't remember the fire. But my back does. Worth it.
Nobody leaves this family. Least of all my oldest friend.
Group hug! Careful, Pim. You're still a flour ghost.
I'm a f-friendly ghost. M-mostly friendly.
Statistically, ghosts don't do group hugs. Pim is the exception.
Then Zeek turns the newspaper over. One more line.
The pot that started the fire was never found.
Big. Black. Three round dents on the side. Like three eyes.
What do you think happens in the next part?
Tell me in the comments.

"불은 기억 안 나. 하지만 내 등은 기억해." — 밥
